- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T15:52:19Z

## PR Description

Completes the host rollout of the owner-approved v3 design: the CLI TUI shipped in #1376; this PR renders the SAME face set in the remaining hosts.

## Shared source (one definition, three renderers)

`lib/src/kaomoji_faces.dart` (pure Dart, only `dart:math`) now owns the approved spec verbatim: the 8 faces (`>_o` `-__` `o_o` `>_<` `o_<` `◕‿◕` `¬_¬` `o_o?` — asymmetric two-eye faces, ASCII fallbacks `^.^` `-_/`), the two-tone brand palette (eyes/strokes teal `#60d0d0`, mouth blue `#70a0e0`), the ~0.9 s random-swap cadence, the approved SVG sprite frames (1.45× content scale, stroke 1.4, `.t`/`.b` classes resolved to inline strokes for flutter_svg), the skip-over face picker (`KaomojiFacePicker`, seedable `Random`; a swap never repeats the showing face) and a `debugPin` fixture seam mirroring the CLI's `FA_KAOMOJI_FACE`. The CLI part file was slimmed to its TUI-side rendering and re-exports the shared names, so all #1376 behavior/tests are unchanged.

## Hosts

1. **App thinking block** (was the head-with-gear `Icons.psychology_outlined`, everywhere): `KaomojiThinkingIcon` renders the SVG sprite frames at 16 px, swapping on a random pick every ~0.9 s while the block streams. New `ChatMessageTile.thinkingLive` gates the animation to the LIVE streaming thinking row — finished thinking notes stay on screen with a frozen face (AC4). Wired in `FaChatScreen`, `FaChatOverlay` and the session sheet (desktop/mobile/web — one widget).
2. **Web TUI / app status row** (the `Working…` analog, `FaRunStatusRow`): the stock spinner is replaced by `KaomojiFaceText` — the kaomoji as two-tone colored spans (teal eyes, blue mouth) in a fixed 4-cell zone, re-picked on the row's existing elapsed ticker (~0.9 s). No new timer anywhere: both hosts animate on Tickers, so the clock stops with the phase (AC4) and no test can end with a pending timer.

## Tests

- `test/kaomoji_faces_test.dart` (core): the 8 faces/ids in the issue order, ASCII fallbacks + mouth segmentation, palette consts, SVG frame invariants (24-grid, 1.45×, 1.4 stroke, both tones, no `class=`), seeded-picker replay determinism, never-repeat + in-range picks, full-coverage run, `debugPin` freeze/clamp, the `kaomojiNextFaceIndex` skip-over seam.
- `packages/fa_ui/test/fa_kaomoji_test.dart` (widget): swapper cadence math (replay twins, no swap before the boundary), `active: false` freeze + mid-run stop, thinking tile renders the sprite (head-with-gear gone) and freezes when the phase ends, live tile swaps on cadence, status row two-tone palette assertion + swap + face gone with the phase.

## Rework round 2 (re-review, 3 rework commits)

- **c2e084e7f** `fix(1374)` — `thinkingLive` now gates on the LIVE thinking message's identity, not the global `isStreaming`: new `liveThinkingMessageIndex` / `liveThinkingMessage` seams on the shared service (`fa_ui`), wired at all three call sites — the chat screen matches by `transcriptIndex` threaded through the custom-message metadata (its tiles rebuild `FaChatMessage`s, so identity can't survive), the overlay and session sheet match with `identical()` against the same `service.messages` list. Regression-tested through the real `FaChatScreen` mapping (two thinking tiles, one boundary: only the newest moves). Also: `KaomojiThinkingIcon.active` defaults **frozen** (public barrel — a forgotten `active:` can no longer start an endless ticker), and `KaomojiFaceText` guards degenerate (empty/whitespace) faces with a plain-span fallback.
- **77bad4283** `test(1374)` — the 3 red widget tests are fixed against the EXACT committed lockfile (flutter_svg 2.3.0): `_shownFace` matches the `ValueKey<KaomojiFace>` box (flutter_svg 2.3.0 mounts its own internal `SizedBox`es → "Too many elements" gone, version-stable), and the status-row test descends `richRoot().children!.single.children` (`Text.rich` nests the given span under a wrapper span, so the old direct read nulled). `packages/fa_ui` is green: 7/7 new tests + the full suite.
- **aaf6fdceb** `refactor(1374)` — the ⚠️ + 💡 threads: status-row face zone scales with the ambient `textScaler`, `_face` opens on the picker's first draw (dead `kKaomojiFaces[0]` literal removed), dead `palette.dim` override removed; TUI `kaomojiEye`/`kaomojiMouth` derive from the shared `kKaomoji*Argb` constants (const bit-splits — cannot drift from the app/web); the core spec test imports the public barrel; the golden regen note is pinned in-repo at `golden_test_helper.dart`.

## Golden mac-regen pass — deterministic and mechanical (⚠️ pending, host-locked)

Goldens stay host-locked (`AGENTS.md`: build-macos/nightly; ubuntu CI never runs them), and this environment has no mac VM — so the pass is pinned, not improvised (same convention as the 0.1.398 release note: "host-locked frames need a macOS `--update-goldens` pass"):

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/golden --update-goldens
git diff --name-only test/golden/goldens   # exactly these 12 must change
```

Determinism: `ensureGoldenFonts` sets `KaomojiFacePicker.debugPin = 0` **before** any frame pumps (also freezing the status row's picker and every thinking tile's swapper — finished tiles mount face 0 frozen, live tiles repaint `>_o` on every boundary), so every regenerated frame is byte-stable `>_o`, regardless of host or run. Expected changed PNGs — exactly 12, nothing else:

- status row (spinner → `KaomojiFaceText`): `goldens/chat/run_status_empty_light`, `run_status_empty_dark`, `run_status_thinking_light`, `run_status_tool_light`, `run_status_tool_dark`
- thinking tile (head-with-gear → `KaomojiThinkingIcon`): `goldens/chat_conversation`, `apps_fa_chat_overlay`, `apps_fa_chat_overlay_light`, `apps_fa_chat_overlay_streaming`, `apps_fa_chat_overlay_streaming_light`, `apps_fa_chat_overlay_rich`, `apps_fa_chat_overlay_rich_ru`

Then eyes on every changed PNG (§Golden tests are MANDATORY step 5) and commit. The list is also pinned in-repo at the `debugPin` seam in `flutter_app/test/golden/golden_test_helper.dart`. No skip flag was introduced: the repo has no standard regen-skip convention, and weakening the mandatory gate for a one-time host-locked pass would rot the next person's tree — the maintainers' mac pass is the repo's own established path.

1. `liveThinkingMessageIndex(service)`: `service.isStreaming ? service.messages.lastIndexWhere((m) => m.role == 'thinking') : -1`.

   - Chat screen: `'transcriptIndex': index` in metadata; `thinkingLive: metadata['transcriptIndex'] == liveThinkingMessageIndex(widget.service)`.
   - Edge: when NOT streaming, `liveThinkingMessageIndex` = -1; `transcriptIndex` for any real message ≥ 0, so no tile matches. Good.
   - Edge: while streaming, `lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking')` — the NEWEST thinking message. Correct per the design (the service appends one thinking message per LLM turn; the newest is the live one while streaming).
   - Edge: what if the transcript has NO thinking message while streaming (e.g., run with no thinking)? `lastIndexWhere` → -1 → nothing animates. Good.
   - Edge: `transcriptIndex` == -1 can never occur since index ≥ 0. Good.

2. Subtle: in the chat screen, the metadata mapping — where does `index` come from? Let me check the mapping function context. The custom messages are mapped from `transcript` (List<FaChatMessage>) — need to confirm `index` is the transcript index matching `service.messages` indices. The metadata mapping is built from `message.metadata` in `_buildCustomMessage`. The mapping source: in `FaChatScreen` build, the transcript is `widget.service.messages`? Let me check how the flutter_chat_ui messages list is derived and whether the `index` in the metadata builder refers to the transcript position. Need to read around line 1040-1100.

3. The metadata `'transcriptIndex'` rides in `metadata['data']`-adjacent space — `data: chat.data` is separate. OK — added key in the custom-message metadata map. Does anything else consume metadata keys in a way this could collide? 'transcriptIndex' is new. Fine.

4. **Potential staleness issue**: `thinkingLive` computed at tile build time. When the streaming phase ENDS, the live tile's `thinkingLive` must flip false. The screen rebuilds on service notify (ListenableBuilder) → the whole chat list rebuilds → thinkingLive becomes false for all. The `KaomojiSwapper.didUpdateWidget` stops the ticker on `active` flip. Good.

5. **Potential issue — overlay/sheet identity across rebuilds**: `liveThinkingMessage(widget.service)` computed per build pass; `messages[index]` from the same list → identical holds. But in the session sheet, `message` — where does it come from? `messages[messageIndex]` — the same list. Good.

6. `FaChatMessage` is mutable (`content` mutable for streaming) but identity is what's compared — fine.

7. What about a thinking message followed by ANOTHER thinking message while streaming (multiple turns)? `lastIndexWhere` → newest. When turn 1's thinking finishes and turn 2's thinking starts, a NEW FaChatMessage is appended (per agent_service_assistant.dart resetting `_currentThinkingMessage`) → new identity → the gate moves. Good.

8. Subtle edge: while streaming, if the newest thinking message belongs to a COMPLETED turn and the current turn streams without thinking (e.g., a tool run after final text)? Then the newest thinking message is NOT live anymore, but `liveThinkingMessageIndex` still returns it (lastIndexWhere finds the newest thinking role regardless of whether it's actually streaming). Actually wait — during a run, after the thinking ends, the assistant message streams in AFTER the thinking message (appended later, higher index). `lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking')` still returns the thinking message's index (the assistant message isn't 'thinking' role). So while the ASSISTANT text streams, the finished thinking tile above it would still be gated `thinkingLive: true` and animate.

The gating fix looks well-designed. Key aspects to scrutinize:

1. `liveThinkingMessageIndex(service)`: `service.isStreaming ? service.messages.lastIndexWhere((m) => m.role == 'thinking') : -1`.
   - Overlay/sheet: `identical(m, liveThinking)` — m is from the SAME `service.messages` list read in the same build pass → identity works.
   - Chat screen: `'transcriptIndex': index` in metadata; `thinkingLive: metadata['transcriptIndex'] == liveThinkingMessageIndex(widget.service)`.
   - Edge: when NOT streaming, `liveThinkingMessageIndex` = -1; `transcriptIndex` for any real message ≥ 0, so no tile matches. Good.
   - Edge: while streaming, `lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking')` — the NEWEST thinking message. Correct per the design (the service appends one thinking message per LLM turn; the newest is the live one while streaming).
   - Edge: what if the transcript has NO thinking message while streaming (e.g., run with no thinking)? `lastIndexWhere` → -1 → nothing animates. Good.
   - Edge: `transcriptIndex` == -1 can never occur since index ≥ 0. Good.

2. Subtle: in the chat screen, the metadata mapping — where does `index` come from? Let me check the mapping function context. The custom messages are mapped from `transcript` (List<FaChatMessage>) — need to confirm `index` is the transcript index matching `service.messages` indices. The metadata mapping is built from `message.metadata` in `_buildCustomMessage`. The mapping source: in `FaChatScreen` build, the transcript is `widget.service.messages`? Let me check how the flutter_chat_ui messages list is derived and whether the `index` in the metadata builder refers to the transcript position. Need to read around line 1040-1100.

3. The metadata `'transcriptIndex'` rides in `metadata['data']`-adjacent space — `data: chat.data` is separate. OK — added key in the custom-message metadata map. Does anything else consume metadata keys in a way this could collide? 'transcriptIndex' is new. Fine.

4. **Potential staleness issue**: `thinkingLive` computed at tile build time. When the streaming phase ENDS, the live tile's `thinkingLive` must flip false. The screen rebuilds on service notify (ListenableBuilder) → the whole chat list rebuilds → thinkingLive becomes false for all. The `KaomojiSwapper.didUpdateWidget` stops the ticker on `active` flip. Good.

5. **Potential issue — overlay/sheet identity across rebuilds**: `liveThinkingMessage(widget.service)` computed per build pass; `messages[index]` from the same list → identical holds. But in the session sheet, `message` — where does it come from? `messages[messageIndex]` — the same list. Good.

6. `FaChatMessage` is mutable (`content` mutable for streaming) but identity is what's compared — fine.

7. What about a thinking message followed by ANOTHER thinking message while streaming (multiple turns)? `lastIndexWhere` → newest. When turn 1's thinking finishes and turn 2's thinking starts, a NEW FaChatMessage is appended (per agent_service_assistant.dart resetting `_currentThinkingMessage`) → new identity → the gate moves. Good.

8. Subtle edge: while streaming, if the newest thinking message belongs to a COMPLETED turn and the current turn streams without thinking (e.g., a tool run after final text)? Then the newest thinking message is NOT live anymore, but `liveThinkingMessageIndex` still returns it (lastIndexWhere finds the newest thinking role regardless of whether it's actually streaming). Hmm — is that a problem? The gate would animate the LAST thinking note even after its turn ended, until the run completes. But that's bounded (one animated tile max, and during a run the most recent thinking IS plausibly the tail of activity). Actually wait — during a run, after the thinking ends, the assistant message streams in AFTER the thinking message (appended later, higher index). `lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking')` still returns the thinking message's index (the assistant message isn't 'thinking' role). So while the ASSISTANT text streams, the finished thinking tile above it would still be gated `thinkingLive: true` and animate.

Hmm — is that a real behavioral regression vs the AC? The intent: "the thinking tile's icon swaps faces ~every 0.9 s while thinking streams, freezes when done". With the index-based gate, the finished thinking tile keeps animating while the assistant response streams (still streaming, just not thinking). The thinking phase ends when the assistant message starts. Is there a finer signal? The prior review's suggested fix direction was exactly this: "expose the streaming thinking message (id) from FaChatService" or "compute 'the newest thinking-role message while streaming' at each call site". The rework implemented the second option — which the reviewer suggested. The imperfection (finished thinking note animating during the assistant-streaming tail of the run) exists in the reviewer's own suggested approach too.

How does the actual service behave? In agent_service_assistant.dart, `_currentThinkingMessage` is reset after each turn — the thinking message gets its final content while the turn is still streaming... The question is whether between thinking-end and run-end, the finished note animates. With one-run-then-idle: during the final assistant streaming, the last thinking note animates. It's a minor residual imperfection, arguably matching "the run is still live" semantics — but NOT matching "freezes when the thinking phase ends" literally.

But hold on — practically, how long is that window? The assistant text streams for the LLM response duration. During that time the finished thinking note visibly swaps faces every 0.9s. Hmm. The PR description says "the thinking tile's icon swaps faces ~every 0.9 s while thinking streams, freezes when done". Strictly, "done" = thinking done, not run done.

Is there a better signal available? `faRunPhase` computes the phase from messages + streaming: `FaRunPhaseKind.writing` when the last message is an assistant text streaming; 'tool' when tools running. The LIVE thinking phase = streaming && the newest message IS the thinking message. A tighter gate: `thinkingLive: streaming && identical(message, service.messages.last)` — only animate when the thinking message IS the newest message. When tools run, the tool messages land after the thinking... then the thinking isn't newest either. Hmm, but during tool runs the thinking note for that turn IS still the "live block" conceptually? No — once tool results arrive, thinking for that turn is done.

Actually — what does the service do with thinking? One thinking message per turn, streamed with deltas, then the assistant message arrives. So "the newest message is the thinking message && streaming" = thinking actively streaming. That would be the tightest gate. The chosen gate ("newest THINKING message while streaming") is looser: it also animates during assistant/tool streaming within the same run.

Severity assessment: the blocker was "EVERY thinking tile animates". Now exactly ONE tile animates per streaming run — the newest thinking note — for the remainder of the run. The flicker of history is gone; one tile animates a bit longer than strictly needed. Tests assert "after one swap boundary only the newest tile's face moved; the finished note stayed frozen" — consistent with the chosen semantics. Is the residual "finished thinking note animates while assistant streams" a blocker? It's a bounded imperfection of the reviewer-suggested approach; AC4's core (idle = no animation; history = no animation) holds. I'd note it as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level observation, not a blocker. Actually, let me check how `faRunPhase` names phases — if during assistant streaming the status row shows "Fa is typing..." and the thinking tile keeps animating, is that visually wrong? Mildly. The strictly-correct gate would be `messages.last is thinking && streaming`. Let me look at run_phase.dart to see what "thinking" phase means there.

Actually, let me check: does `faRunPhase` even have a 'thinking' kind distinct from writing? From the status row code: `FaRunPhaseKind.writing` → "Fa is typing..."; tool → tool name; `_` (default, incl. thinking) → `chatStatusThinking`. So t…

blocks.text:
The gating fix looks well-designed. Key aspects to scrutinize:

1. `liveThinkingMessageIndex(service)`: `service.isStreaming ? service.messages.lastIndexWhere((m) => m.role == 'thinking') : -1`.
   - Overlay/sheet: `identical(m, liveThinking)` — m is from the SAME `service.messages` list read in the same build pass → identity works.
   - Chat screen: `'transcriptIndex': index` in metadata; `thinkingLive: metadata['transcriptIndex'] == liveThinkingMessageIndex(widget.service)`.
   - Edge: when NOT streaming, `liveThinkingMessageIndex` = -1; `transcriptIndex` for any real message ≥ 0, so no tile matches. Good.
   - Edge: while streaming, `lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking')` — the NEWEST thinking message. Correct per the design (the service appends one thinking message per LLM turn; the newest is the live one while streaming).
   - Edge: what if the transcript has NO thinking message while streaming (e.g., run with no thinking)? `lastIndexWhere` → -1 → nothing animates. Good.
   - Edge: `transcriptIndex` == -1 can never occur since index ≥ 0. Good.

2. Subtle: in the chat screen, the metadata mapping — where does `index` come from? Let me check the mapping function context. The custom messages are mapped from `transcript` (List<FaChatMessage>) — need to confirm `index` is the transcript index matching `service.messages` indices. The metadata mapping is built from `message.metadata` in `_buildCustomMessage`. The mapping source: in `FaChatScreen` build, the transcript is `widget.service.messages`? Let me check how the flutter_chat_ui messages list is derived and whether the `index` in the metadata builder refers to the transcript position. Need to read around line 1040-1100.

3. The metadata `'transcriptIndex'` rides in `metadata['data']`-adjacent space — `data: chat.data` is separate. OK — added key in the custom-message metadata map. Does anything else consume metadata keys in a way this could collide? 'transcriptIndex' is new. Fine.

4. **Potential staleness issue**: `thinkingLive` computed at tile build time. When the streaming phase ENDS, the live tile's `thinkingLive` must flip false. The screen rebuilds on service notify (ListenableBuilder) → the whole chat list rebuilds → thinkingLive becomes false for all. The `KaomojiSwapper.didUpdateWidget` stops the ticker on `active` flip. Good.

5. **Potential issue — overlay/sheet identity across rebuilds**: `liveThinkingMessage(widget.service)` computed per build pass; `messages[index]` from the same list → identical holds. But in the session sheet, `message` — where does it come from? `messages[messageIndex]` — the same list. Good.

6. `FaChatMessage` is mutable (`content` mutable for streaming) but identity is what's compared — fine.

7. What about a thinking message followed by ANOTHER thinking message while streaming (multiple turns)? `lastIndexWhere` → newest. When turn 1's thinking finishes and turn 2's thinking starts, a NEW FaChatMessage is appended (per agent_service_assistant.dart resetting `_currentThinkingMessage`) → new identity → the gate moves. Good.

8. Subtle edge: while streaming, if the newest thinking message belongs to a COMPLETED turn and the current turn streams without thinking (e.g., a tool run after final text)? Then the newest thinking message is NOT live anymore, but `liveThinkingMessageIndex` still returns it (lastIndexWhere finds the newest thinking role regardless of whether it's actually streaming). Hmm — is that a problem? The gate would animate the LAST thinking note even after its turn ended, until the run completes. But that's bounded (one animated tile max, and during a run the most recent thinking IS plausibly the tail of activity). Actually wait — during a run, after the thinking ends, the assistant message streams in AFTER the thinking message (appended later, higher index). `lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking')` still returns the thinking message's index (the assistant message isn't 'thinking' role). So while the ASSISTANT text streams, the finished thinking tile above it would still be gated `thinkingLive: true` and animate.

Hmm — is that a real behavioral regression vs the AC? The intent: "the thinking tile's icon swaps faces ~every 0.9 s while thinking streams, freezes when done". With the index-based gate, the finished thinking tile keeps animating while the assistant response streams (still streaming, just not thinking). The thinking phase ends when the assistant message starts. Is there a finer signal? The prior review's suggested fix direction was exactly this: "expose the streaming thinking message (id) from FaChatService" or "compute 'the newest thinking-role message while streaming' at each call site". The rework implemented the second option — which the reviewer suggested. The imperfection (finished thinking note animating during the assistant-streaming tail of the run) exists in the reviewer's own suggested approach too.

How does the actual service behave? In agent_service_assistant.dart, `_currentThinkingMessage` is reset after each turn — the thinking message gets its final content while the turn is still streaming... The question is whether between thinking-end and run-end, the finished note animates. With one-run-then-idle: during the final assistant streaming, the last thinking note animates. It's a minor residual imperfection, arguably matching "the run is still live" semantics — but NOT matching "freezes when the thinking phase ends" literally.

But hold on — practically, how long is that window? The assistant text streams for the LLM response duration. During that time the finished thinking note visibly swaps faces every 0.9s. Hmm. The PR description says "the thinking tile's icon swaps faces ~every 0.9 s while thinking streams, freezes when done". Strictly, "done" = thinking done, not run done.

Is there a better signal available? `faRunPhase` computes the phase from messages + streaming: `FaRunPhaseKind.writing` when the last message is an assistant text streaming; 'tool' when tools running. The LIVE thinking phase = streaming && the newest message IS the thinking message. A tighter gate: `thinkingLive: streaming && identical(message, service.messages.last)` — only animate when the thinking message IS the newest message. When tools run, the tool messages land after the thinking... then the thinking isn't newest either. Hmm, but during tool runs the thinking note for that turn IS still the "live block" conceptually? No — once tool results arrive, thinking for that turn is done.

Actually — what does the service do with thinking? One thinking message per turn, streamed with deltas, then the assistant message arrives. So "the newest message is the thinking message && streaming" = thinking actively streaming. That would be the tightest gate. The chosen gate ("newest THINKING message while streaming") is looser: it also animates during assistant/tool streaming within the same run.

Severity assessment: the blocker was "EVERY thinking tile animates". Now exactly ONE tile animates per streaming run — the newest thinking note — for the remainder of the run. The flicker of history is gone; one tile animates a bit longer than strictly needed. Tests assert "after one swap boundary only the newest tile's face moved; the finished note stayed frozen" — consistent with the chosen semantics. Is the residual "finished thinking note animates while assistant streams" a blocker? It's a bounded imperfection of the reviewer-suggested approach; AC4's core (idle = no animation; history = no animation) holds. I'd note it as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level observation, not a blocker. Actually, let me check how `faRunPhase` names phases — if during assistant streaming the status row shows "Fa is typing..." and the thinking tile keeps animating, is that visually wrong? Mildly. The strictly-correct gate would be `messages.last is thinking && streaming`. Let me look at run_phase.dart to see what "thinking" phase means there.

Actually, let me check: does `faRunPhase` even have a 'thinking' kind distinct from writing? From the status row code: `FaRunPhaseKind.writing` → "Fa is typing..."; tool → tool name; `_` (default, incl. thinking) → `chatStatusThinking`. So t…

The FINISHED thinking tile's face CHANGED across the swap boundary. So either:
(a) The test is flaky/environment-dependent, or
(b) The wiring actually animates BOTH tiles — the fix doesn't work as claimed.

Let me analyze the test:
```dart
final service = _TranscriptService()
  ..msgs = [thinking(finished), user, thinking(live)]
  ..streaming = true;
await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(home: FaChatScreen(service: service)));
await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 1));
await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));
expect(_faces(tester), hasLength(2));
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);

expect(after[0], same(before[0]), reason: 'finished frozen');
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])), reason: 'live animates');
```

`_faces` returns widgetList of keyed boxes in tree order. `after[0]` = the finished tile's face.

Why would the finished tile's face change? Possibilities:

1. **The transcript sync rebuilds tiles with NEW KaomojiSwapper states**: The FaChatScreen maps the transcript through `_toMessage` with a 50ms debounce; tiles keyed by `message.id` ('msg-0', 'msg-2'). If the transcript list rebuilds and the ChatMessageTile element is preserved (same key), the KaomojiSwapper state persists and the frozen tile's ticker is stopped (thinkingLive false)... its face shouldn't change.

2. **`widget rebuild` → new `KaomojiSwapper` with different `random`**: When a ChatMessageTile rebuilds (didUpdateWidget), the Swapper widget is recreated — `random` is null (production path — ChatMessageTile creates `KaomojiThinkingIcon(size: 16, active: thinkingLive)` with no random). The STATE persists (same element), `_face` persists. Ticker stopped. Face frozen. Fine.

3. **The finished tile was NOT actually gated off**: maybe `transcriptIndex` doesn't match — wait, if the gate is broken the OTHER way (finished tile animating), after[0] changes. Tile 2 → true. Hmm.

If the whole list re-mounts every frame, both faces re-randomize and the test would fail at line 335 (first assertion). Also `after[1] isNot same(before[1])` would usually pass. So the symptom matches "the finished tile's swapper state was recreated" — i.e., the transcript sync/element tree churns and the finished tile remounts between `before` and `after` pumps.

Between `before` and `after` pumps, if a rebuild swapped the WIDGET instances (new ValueKey(same face) → same instance value), `same()` compares the VALUE (KaomojiFace identity — const instances). The ValueKey's value is the face. If the state persists and no swap occurs, the same const KaomojiFace instance appears → same() holds.

For a ListView with reverse:true, children in tree order are still built by index... the display order doesn't change the finder's tree order (it follows the element tree: first child = first built). With `reverse: true`, the FIRST built child is the LAST item? So **the FINISHED tile's swapper has `active: true`** and the LIVE tile's swapper has `active: false`?? That's INVERTED from expectations. And `after1 != before1` — wait, the probe shows `identical(after[1], before[1]): true` — face[1] did NOT move, while face[0] DID move (false). So actually THE FIRST TILE (finished note, msgs[0]) is the ANIMATING one, and the SECOND (live turn, msgs[2]) is FROZEN!

The gate is INVERTED: the finished note animates; the live note freezes. That's why the wiring test fails at line 335 (`after[0] same before[0]` fails).

Why inverted? `liveThinkingMessageIndex` = `msgs.lastIndexWhere((m) => m.role == 'thinking')` = 2 → the live gate should be transcriptIndex 2 (the LAST tile). In tree order, which tile is first? If the transcript renders NEWEST-FIRST (reverse display, common for chat lists — flutter_chat_ui lists are often reversed with newest at index 0 visually at bottom)... In TREE order with a reversed list, the FIRST built child is... SliverList builds children index order of the list; with `reverse: true`, the FIRST list index is painted at the viewport's bottom. Element tree order still follows child index. So if the chat list is REVERSED (newest first in the widget list), tree-order[0] = msgs[2] (the LIVE one) and tree-order[1] = msgs[0] (finished).

The probe says swapper[0].active == true → tree-order[0] = the gated-live tile = msgs[2] (live turn) — CORRECT gating! And `_faces[0]` = msgs[2]'s face — which moved across the boundary (correct, it's live). `_faces[1]` = msgs[0] (finished) — frozen (correct!).

So THE WIRING IS CORRECT — the TEST's assumption about tree order is wrong! The test asserts `_faces[0]` is the finished note, but `_faces[0]` is actually the live note (the transcript renders newest-first in tree order).

Let me double-check with the face identities: warm faces [13622522, 38ca3a69]; after a boundary, faces[0] changed identity. The live tile animates → face[0] = live tile ✓ consistent with newest-first tree order.

But wait — visually, which is on screen where doesn't matter. The important part: swapper active flags [true, false] = [msgs[2] live, msgs[0] finished] — the GATE IS CORRECT. Only the TEST's index assumption is inverted.

Hmm, hold on — let me be careful: is tree-order[0] really msgs[2]? The transcript has 3 messages: thinking(0), user(1), thinking(2). The chat list renders ALL THREE, but only 2 thinking tiles exist. If the list is reversed (newest first in child order): children = [msgs[2]-thinking, msgs[1]-user, msgs[0]-thinking]. Tree order of keyed boxes: msgs[2]'s face first, then msgs[0]'s. blocks.text:
Confirmed: `widget.service.messages.indexed.map((entry) => _toMessage(entry.$1, entry.$2))` — the index IS the position in `service.messages`, 1:1, no filtering. The index-based gate is correct.

Now let me check the remaining verification items:
1. The full fa_ui suite result (background job running).
2. Core test + CLI kaomoji tests.
3. The chat screen gate: `liveThinkingMessageIndex(widget.service)` is computed inside `_buildCustomMessage` — per tile build. Fine.

One more correctness check on the chat screen: `_buildCustomMessage` — the metadata map is built at `_toMessage` time (transcript sync, 50ms debounce). `transcriptIndex` is stable per message. And `liveThinkingMessageIndex` re-evaluated per tile build. When streaming ends, notify → rebuild → no match → freeze.

Edge: `_messageChanged` compares `customA.metadata?.toString()` — the added 'transcriptIndex' key participates in metadata.toString() — no behavioral issue.

Another subtle point: the overlay/sheet `identical()` gate — `liveThinkingMessage()` reads `service.messages` in the build closure; the tiles receive `messages[index]` from the SAME list reference (captured in the builder). If the service REPLACES the messages list between notify and rebuild, both read the new list in the same pass. OK.

Now, is there any issue with the CHAT SCREEN's `liveThinkingMessageIndex` when `messages` is being mutated (a new thinking message appended mid-stream)? lastIndexWhere on the live list — fine.

Now, the residual imperfection I identified: while streaming, after the thinking phase ends (assistant text streaming), the newest thinking note still matches `lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking')` and keeps animating until the run ends. How does the REAL service sequence messages? Let me check agent_service_assistant.dart to see: during a run — user msg → thinking msg (streamed) → assistant msg (streamed) → possibly tool messages → ... The gate animates the last thinking note while ANY of that streams. The prior review's suggested direction was exactly "compute 'the newest thinking-role message while streaming'" — the rework implemented precisely that. So the residual behavior matches the reviewer's own suggested fix. The AC4 concern (history flicker, N tickers) is resolved: exactly ≤1 tile animates during a run.

Is the residual worth flagging? The thinking tile animating while the assistant text streams below it — the "Thinking…" tile face keeps swapping while "Fa is typing..." shows in the status row. Mildly odd but arguably intentional ("the run is live, the last thinking block is the freshest agent activity"). Since the previous round's own fix direction produces exactly this, and the PR's AC4 statement ("finished thinking notes stay on screen with a frozen face") is satisfied for all-but-one note... hmm, "finished thinking notes stay on screen with a frozen face" — the newest note is "finished" (its content is complete) once the assistant message starts. Strictly read, that one note still animates. But the wire test asserts the chosen semantics, and it matches the round-2 recommendation verbatim.

Decision: flag as a 💡 SUGGESTION (tighten to `messages.last` when the last message is the thinking one, or gate via `faRunPhase`'s thinking-kind), NOT a blocker. It does not contradict the blocker's fix (history frozen, ≤1 ticker), and the suggested fix was implemented as directed. Actually — hmm, let me think again about whether this is IMPORTANT. The AC4 as stated in the PR description: "finished thinking notes stay on screen with a frozen face (AC4)". If the newest thinking note animates during the assistant-streaming tail, then a "finished" note (content-wise) is not frozen. But practically: while streaming, is there a state where the newest thinking message's content is final AND the run is still streaming AND no newer thinking exists? Yes — the assistant text streaming phase. Duration: the LLM response streaming time (seconds to minutes for long answers). During that whole window the last thinking tile animates.

Hmm, but is that visually wrong? The tile header says "Thinking" — if the face keeps swapping, it suggests the agent is still thinking when it's actually typing the answer. The status row correctly switches to "Fa is typing..." (writing phase). So there IS a visible inconsistency: status row says typing, thinking tile animates.

I could suggest: gate via the run phase — `faRunPhase(streaming: ..., messages: ...)` yields FaRunPhaseKind; thinkingLive should be true only when the phase is the thinking-ish default kind AND the message is the newest thinking one. Actually simpler: `thinkingLive: streaming && identical/… && message index == messages.length - 1` — only animate when the thinking block IS the newest transcript entry (nothing has landed after it). The FINISHED thinking tile's face CHANGED across the swap boundary. So either:
(a) The test is flaky/environment-dependent, or
(b) The wiring actually animates BOTH tiles — the fix doesn't work as claimed.

Let me analyze the test:
```dart
final service = _TranscriptService()
  ..msgs = [thinking(finished), user, thinking(live)]
  ..streaming = true;
await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(home: FaChatScreen(service: service)));
await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 1));
await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));
expect(_faces(tester), hasLength(2));
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);

expect(after[0], same(before[0]), reason: 'finished frozen');
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])), reason: 'live animates');
```

`_faces` returns widgetList of keyed boxes in tree order. `after[0]` = the finished tile's face.

Why would the finished tile's face change? Possibilities:

1. **The transcript sync rebuilds tiles with NEW KaomojiSwapper states**: The FaChatScreen maps the transcript through `_toMessage` with a 50ms debounce; tiles keyed by `message.id` ('msg-0', 'msg-2'). If the transcript list rebuilds and the ChatMessageTile element is preserved (same key), the KaomojiSwapper state persists and the frozen tile's ticker is stopped (thinkingLive false)... its face shouldn't change.

2. **`widget rebuild` → new `KaomojiSwapper` with different `random`**: When a ChatMessageTile rebuilds (didUpdateWidget), the Swapper widget is recreated — `random` is null (production path — ChatMessageTile creates `KaomojiThinkingIcon(size: 16, active: thinkingLive)` with no random). The STATE persists (same element), `_face` persists. Ticker stopped. Face frozen. Fine.

3. **The finished tile was NOT actually gated off**: maybe `transcriptIndex` doesn't match — wait, if the gate is broken the OTHER way (finished tile animating), after[0] changes. Tile 2 → true. Hmm.

If the whole list re-mounts every frame, both faces re-randomize and the test would fail at line 335 (first assertion). Also `after[1] isNot same(before[1])` would usually pass. So the symptom matches "the finished tile's swapper state was recreated" — i.e., the transcript sync/element tree churns and the finished tile remounts between `before` and `after` pumps.

Between `before` and `after` pumps, if a rebuild swapped the WIDGET instances (new ValueKey(same face) → same instance value), `same()` compares the VALUE (KaomojiFace identity — const instances). The ValueKey's value is the face. If the state persists and no swap occurs, the same const KaomojiFace instance appears → same() holds.

For a ListView with reverse:true, children in tree order are still built by index... the display order doesn't change the finder's tree order (it follows the element tree: first child = first built). With `reverse: true`, the FIRST built child is the LAST item? The FINISHED thinking tile's face CHANGED across the swap boundary. So either:
(a) The test is flaky/environment-dependent, or
(b) The wiring actually animates BOTH tiles — the fix doesn't work as claimed.

Let me analyze the test:
```dart
final service = _TranscriptService()
  ..msgs = [thinking(finished), user, thinking(live)]
  ..streaming = true;
await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(home: FaChatScreen(service: service)));
await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 1));
await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));
expect(_faces(tester), hasLength(2));
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
final after = _faces(tester);
expect(after[0], same(before[0]), reason: 'finished frozen');
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])), reason: 'live animates');
```

`_faces` returns widgetList of keyed boxes in tree order. `after[0]` = the finished tile's face.

Why would the finished tile's face change? Possibilities:

1. **The transcript sync rebuilds tiles with NEW KaomojiSwapper states**: The FaChatScreen maps the transcript through `_toMessage` with a 50ms debounce; tiles keyed by `message.id` ('msg-0', 'msg-2'). If the transcript list rebuilds and the ChatMessageTile element is preserved (same key), the KaomojiSwapper state persists and the frozen tile's ticker is stopped (thinkingLive false)... its face shouldn't change.

2. **`widget rebuild` → new `KaomojiSwapper` with different `random`**: When a ChatMessageTile rebuilds (didUpdateWidget), the Swapper widget is recreated — `random` is null (production path — ChatMessageTile creates `KaomojiThinkingIcon(size: 16, active: thinkingLive)` with no random). The STATE persists (same element), `_face` persists. Ticker stopped. Face frozen. Fine.

3. **The finished tile was NOT actually gated off**: maybe `transcriptIndex` doesn't match — wait, if the gate is broken the OTHER way (finished tile animating), after[0] changes. What if `liveThinkingMessageIndex` returns index 0?? `msgs = [thinking, user, thinking]`, lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking') = 2. Tile 0's metadata transcriptIndex = 0 ≠ 2 → thinkingLive false. Confirmed: the ONLY failure in the whole `packages/fa_ui` suite (569 passed / 1 failed) is the rework's own new **wiring regression test**:

```
wiring (AC4): only the NEWEST thinking tile animates while a run streams — finished notes stay frozen
Expected: same instance as <KaomojiFace>
Actual: <KaomojiFace>
at fa_kaomoji_test.dart:335 — `expect(after[0], same(before[0]), reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face')`
```

The FINISHED thinking tile's face CHANGED across the swap boundary. So either:
(a) The test is flaky/environment-dependent, or
(b) The wiring actually animates BOTH tiles — the fix doesn't work as claimed.

Let me analyze the test:
```dart
final service = _TranscriptService()
  ..msgs = [thinking(finished), user, thinking(live)]
  ..streaming = true;
await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(home: FaChatScreen(service: service)));
await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 1));
await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));
expect(_faces(tester), hasLength(2));
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
final after = _faces(tester);
expect(after[0], same(before[0]), reason: 'finished frozen');
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])), reason: 'live animates');
```

`_faces` returns widgetList of keyed boxes in tree order. `after[0]` = the finished tile's face.

Why would the finished tile's face change? Possibilities:

1. **The transcript sync rebuilds tiles with NEW KaomojiSwapper states**: The FaChatScreen maps the transcript through `_toMessage` with a 50ms debounce; tiles keyed by `message.id` ('msg-0', 'msg-2'). If the transcript list rebuilds and the ChatMessageTile element is preserved (same key), the KaomojiSwapper state persists and the frozen tile's ticker is stopped (thinkingLive false)... its face shouldn't change.

2. **`widget rebuild` → new `KaomojiSwapper` with different `random`**: When a ChatMessageTile rebuilds (didUpdateWidget), the Swapper widget is recreated — `random` is null (production path — ChatMessageTile creates `KaomojiThinkingIcon(size: 16, active: thinkingLive)` with no random). The STATE persists (same element), `_face` persists. Ticker stopped. Face frozen. Fine.

3. **The finished tile was NOT actually gated off**: maybe `transcriptIndex` doesn't match — wait, if the gate is broken the OTHER way (finished tile animating), after[0] changes. What if `liveThinkingMessageIndex` returns index 0?? `msgs = [thinking, user, thinking]`, lastIndexWhere(role == 'thinking') = 2. Tile 0's metadata transcriptIndex = 0 ≠ 2 → thinkingLive false. Tile 2 → true. Hmm.

4. **Both tiles re-mount fresh** (element tree rebuilt, new states): Then the finished tile would get a NEW KaomojiSwapper → `_picker.first()` → a NEW RANDOM face — `after[0]` likely ≠ `before[0]` (same-instance check fails: `same()` compares identity; a fresh `_picker.first()` returns the SAME const instance if the same face index is drawn — 1/8 chance same instance). If the whole list re-mounts every frame, both faces re-randomize and the test would fail at line 335 (first assertion). Also `after[1] isNot same(before[1])` would usually pass. So the symptom matches "the finished tile's swapper state was recreated" — i.e., the transcript sync/element tree churns and the finished tile remounts between `before` and `after` pumps.

Why would it remount? The `_KeepAlive`/debounce sync — during the pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod), does the transcript re-sync (timer-based debounce) and produce NEW Message objects ('msg-0' CustomMessage recreated)? The chat list (`flutter_chat_ui`) keys messages by id — `Message.custom(id: 'msg-0')` recreated but same id → element preserved. Unless the PARENT of the tile changes identity in a way that remounts children...

Hmm wait — actually, let me reconsider. `_faces(tester)` — `tester.widgetList(find.byWidgetPredicate(...))` returns the CURRENT widget configurations in tree order. Between `before` and `after` pumps, if a rebuild swapped the WIDGET instances (new ValueKey(same face) → same instance value), `same()` compares the VALUE (KaomojiFace identity — const instances). The ValueKey's value is the face. If the state persists and no swap occurs, the same const KaomojiFace instance appears → same() holds.

BUT — `ChatMessageTile` has a "reveal gate" and COLLAPSING behavior: long thinking content collapses to head/tail. Hmm, content 'finished turn' is short.

Another candidate: **the `pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod)` triggers the transcript's periodic reveal/scroll** — no.

Actually, the simplest explanation: **the whole transcript DID re-sync during the boundary pump** (the 50ms debounce timer from the initial mount fires... no, we pumped 1s + 100ms already before `before`).

Wait — `pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod)` = pump 900ms in ONE call. During a single pump(duration) with animations, ONLY ONE frame is produced at the END of the duration. Tickers fire once. Timers (debounce) with less remaining time fire. What timers exist at that point? The transcript sync debounce already fired (1s pump). Any other periodic behavior in FaChatScreen? A "thinking" auto-scroll? The reveal gate?

Hmm — alternatively the failure could be REAL: the finished tile animates because `thinkingLive` for tile 0 is TRUE. How? `liveThinkingMessageIndex(widget.service)`... wait — `widget.service` in `_FaChatScreenState` — is it the SAME service the test passes? Yes. `isStreaming` true. `msgs` lastIndexWhere thinking → 2. Tile 0 metadata transcriptIndex 0. 0 == 2 false → thinkingLive false.

Unless... the metadata mapping assigns transcriptIndex = the index in the CHAT-UI list, which for CustomMessage building is `messages.indexed` — the transcript list INCLUDING user messages: index 0 = thinking, 1 = user, 2 = thinking. ✓.

Hmm, but wait: does the chat screen REVERSE the list for display (flutter_chat_ui often reverses)? `_toMessage(index, chat)` — index from `widget.service.messages.indexed` — chronological. Tile identity by id 'msg-N'. The `transcriptIndex` rides in metadata — correct value regardless of display order.

OK here's another thought — **`_faces` tree order**: `tester.widgetList` in tree order. In a REVERSED display list (newest at bottom = index 2 rendered LAST in tree order?), `_faces(tester)` order... For a ListView with reverse:true, children in tree order are still built by index... the display order doesn't change the finder's tree order (it follows the element tree: first child = first built). With `reverse: true`, the FIRST built child is the LAST item? ListView reverse builds children... the SliverList builds index order regardless of reverse; the PAINT/PHYSICS is reversed. widgetList order follows element order = index order = msgs[0] first, msgs[2] last. So `_faces[0]` = finished note (msgs[0]), `_faces[1]` = live (msgs[2]). The test asserts after[0] frozen, after[1] moved.

The failure says after[0] != before[0] — the finished note MOVED. So either the finished note animated (gate broken for tile 0) or its swapper remounted.

Let me just probe: modify nothing; write a quick standalone probe test to diagnose. Actually — simpler: is this test ORDER-dependent or FLAKY? The test ran `+8 -1` — it failed deterministically in both the full suite AND the isolated file run. So it's deterministic on this machine/toolchain.

Could it be a RANDOM issue? The finished tile has NO injected random (production KaomojiSwapper uses Random() unseed). If the finished tile's swapper remounts or ticks... The live tile animates with a random picker; the finished is frozen. If the gate were broken (tile 0 live too), BOTH faces would move — after[0] isNot(before[0]) with high probability (7/8), failing `same()` deterministically-enough. Two consecutive failures — could be 1/64 luck, but more likely the gate IS broken for tile 0.

How could tile 0 be live? If `liveThinkingMessageIndex` were 0 — i.e., `msgs` lastIndexWhere thinking = 0?? That would require the service to see a DIFFERENT list — e.g., FaChatScreen COPIES/filters messages... OR `_TranscriptService.msgs` reassigned... no.

Confirmed: the ONLY failure in the whole `packages/fa_ui` suite (569 passed / 1 failed) is the rework's own new **wiring regression test**:

```
wiring (AC4): only the NEWEST thinking tile animates while a run streams — finished notes stay frozen
Expected: same instance as <KaomojiFace>
Actual: <KaomojiFace>
at fa_kaomoji_test.dart:335 — `expect(after[0], same(before[0]), reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face')`
```

The FINISHED thinking tile's face CHANGED across the swap boundary. So either:
(a) The test is flaky/environment-dependent, or
(b) The wiring actually animates BOTH tiles — the fix doesn't work as claimed.

Let me analyze the test:
```dart
final service = _TranscriptService()
  ..msgs = [thinking(finished), user, thinking(live)]
  ..streaming = true;
await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(home: FaChatScreen(service: service)));
await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 1));
await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));
expect(_faces(tester), hasLength(2));
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
final after = _faces(tester);
expect(after[0], same(before[0]), reason: 'finished frozen');
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])), reason: 'live animates');
```

`_faces` returns widgetList of keyed boxes in tree order. `after[0]` = the finished tile's face.

Why would the finished tile's face change? Possibilities:

1. **The transcript sync rebuilds tiles with NEW KaomojiSwapper states**: The FaChatScreen maps the transcript through `_toMessage` with a 50ms debounce; tiles keyed by `message.id` ('msg-0', 'msg-2'). The FINISHED thinking tile's face CHANGED across the swap boundary. So either:
(a) The test is flaky/environment-dependent, or
(b) The wiring actually animates BOTH tiles — the fix doesn't work as claimed.

Let me analyze the test:
```dart
final service = _TranscriptService()
  ..msgs = [thinking(finished), user, thinking(live)]
  ..streaming = true;
await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(home: FaChatScreen(service: service)));
await tester.pump(const Duration(seconds: 1));
await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 100));
expect(_faces(tester), hasLength(2));
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);

expect(after[0], same(before[0]), reason: 'finished frozen');
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])), reason: 'live animates');
```

`_faces` returns widgetList of keyed boxes in tree order. `after[0]` = the finished tile's face.

Why would the finished tile's face change? Possibilities:

1. **The transcript sync rebuilds tiles with NEW KaomojiSwapper states**: The FaChatScreen maps the transcript through `_toMessage` with a 50ms debounce; tiles keyed by `message.id` ('msg-0', 'msg-2'). If the transcript list rebuilds and the ChatMessageTile element is preserved (same key), the KaomojiSwapper state persists and the frozen tile's ticker is stopped (thinkingLive false)... its face shouldn't change.

2. **`widget rebuild` → new `KaomojiSwapper` with different `random`**: When a ChatMessageTile rebuilds (didUpdateWidget), the Swapper widget is recreated — `random` is null (production path — ChatMessageTile creates `KaomojiThinkingIcon(size: 16, active: thinkingLive)` with no random). The STATE persists (same element), `_face` persists. Ticker stopped. Face frozen. Fine.

3. **The finished tile was NOT actually gated off**: maybe `transcriptIndex` doesn't match — wait, if the gate is broken the OTHER way (finished tile animating), after[0] changes. Tile 2 → true. Hmm.

If the whole list re-mounts every frame, both faces re-randomize and the test would fail at line 335 (first assertion). Also `after[1] isNot same(before[1])` would usually pass. So the symptom matches "the finished tile's swapper state was recreated" — i.e., the transcript sync/element tree churns and the finished tile remounts between `before` and `after` pumps.

Between `before` and `after` pumps, if a rebuild swapped the WIDGET instances (new ValueKey(same face) → same instance value), `same()` compares the VALUE (KaomojiFace identity — const instances). The ValueKey's value is the face. If the state persists and no swap occurs, the same const KaomojiFace instance appears → same() holds.

For a ListView with reverse:true, children in tree order are still built by index... the display order doesn't change the finder's tree order (it follows the element tree: first child = first built). With `reverse: true`, the FIRST built child is the LAST item? PROBE swappers mounted: 2   active flags: [true, false]

The transcript list renders **newest-first in tree order** (reversed display list), so `_faces[0]` is the LIVE thinking tile and `_faces[1]` is the finished note — the exact opposite of what the assertions assume:

```dart
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
final after = _faces(tester);
expect(after[0], same(before[0]),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face'); // ← [0] IS the live tile
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');            // ← [1] is the frozen one
```

```dart
KaomojiFace shown(bool liveActive) =>
    (tester.widget(find.descendant(
      of: find.byWidgetPredicate(
          (w) => w is KaomojiSwapper && w.active == liveActive),
      matching: find.byWidgetPredicate((w) => w.key is ValueKey<KaomojiFace>),
    )).key! as ValueKey<KaomojiFace>).value;

expect(tester.widgetList<KaomojiSwapper>(find.byType(KaomojiSwapper)),
    hasLength(2));
final liveBefore = shown(true);
final finishedBefore = shown(false);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
expect(shown(false), same(finishedBefore),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face');
expect(shown(true), isNot(same(liveBefore)),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');
```

```

flutter test test/fa_kaomoji_test.dart                             → 9 passed, 1 failed

```

The only red test in the package is this PR's new `wiring (AC4)` test. A runtime probe of the exact same tree (two thinking tiles through the real `FaChatScreen`, one pump past the swap boundary) shows **the gate itself works**:

```
PROBE swappers mounted: 2   active flags: [true, false]
PROBE face[0] moved across the boundary  (the LIVE tile)
PROBE face[1] identical before/after     (the finished note — frozen)
```

The transcript list renders **newest-first in tree order** (reversed display list), so `_faces[0]` is the LIVE thinking tile and `_faces[1]` is the finished note — the exact opposite of what the assertions assume:

```dart
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
final after = _faces(tester);
expect(after[0], same(before[0]),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face'); // ← [0] IS the live tile
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');            // ← [1] is the frozen one
```

Fix: identify the tiles by the gate itself instead of by position — it's also a stronger assertion of the actual contract (exactly one live swapper):

```dart
KaomojiFace shown(bool liveActive) =>
    (tester.widget(find.descendant(
      of: find.byWidgetPredicate(
          (w) => w is KaomojiSwapper && w.active == liveActive),
      matching: find.byWidgetPredicate((w) => w.key is ValueKey<KaomojiFace>),
    )).key! as ValueKey<KaomojiFace>).value;

expect(tester.widgetList<KaomojiSwapper>(find.byType(KaomojiSwapper)),
    hasLength(2));
final liveBefore = shown(true);
final finishedBefore = shown(false);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
expect(shown(false), same(finishedBefore),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face');
expect(shown(true), isNot(same(liveBefore)),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');
```

(`KaomojiSwapper` is public through the `fa_ui` barrel; matching by the `active` flag is stable across the boundary rebuild, unlike widget-instance lookups.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the live gate keeps the newest thinking note animating through the whole run, not just while it streams**

`liveThinkingMessageIndex` returns the newest `thinking`-role message for as long as `isStreaming` — including the phases after that block finished: while the assistant text streams in below it (the status row already switched to «Fa is typing...») and while tool rows run, the newest thinking tile keeps swapping faces every ~0.9 s. A finished (content-complete) thinking note is therefore not always frozen, which is a strict reading of the PR's own AC4 wording.

This matches the round-2 fix direction ("the newest thinking-role message while streaming") and the CLI busy row's semantics (the face marks "agent at work" for the whole busy period), so it's a defensible call — flagging only the stricter alternative if the owner wants freeze-on-phase-end semantics: additionally require the thinking block to be the transcript tail (`index == service.messages.length - 1`) or gate through `faRunPhase`'s thinking kind, so the note freezes the frame the phase moves past it.       matching: find.byWidgetPredicate((w) => w.key is ValueKey<KaomojiFace>),

expect(shown(false), same(finishedBefore),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face');
expect(shown(true), isNot(same(liveBefore)),

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the rework's own wiring regression test fails deterministically — the gate is correct, the test's tree-order assumption is inverted**

Re-verified on head `aaf6fdceb` (Flutter 3.47.6, committed lockfile):

```
flutter test                            (packages/fa_ui full suite) → 569 passed, 1 failed
flutter test test/fa_kaomoji_test.dart                             → 9 passed, 1 failed

Expected: same instance as <Instance of 'KaomojiFace'>
  Actual: <Instance of 'KaomojiFace'>
  the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face   ← fa_kaomoji_test.dart:335
```

The only red test in the package is this PR's new `wiring (AC4)` test. A runtime probe of the exact same tree (two thinking tiles through the real `FaChatScreen`, one pump past the swap boundary) shows **the gate itself works**:

```
PROBE swappers mounted: 2   active flags: [true, false]
PROBE face[0] moved across the boundary  (the LIVE tile)
PROBE face[1] identical before/after     (the finished note — frozen)
```

The transcript list renders **newest-first in tree order** (reversed display list), so `_faces[0]` is the LIVE thinking tile and `_faces[1]` is the finished note — the exact opposite of what the assertions assume:

```dart
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
final after = _faces(tester);
expect(after[0], same(before[0]),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face'); // ← [0] IS the live tile
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');            // ← [1] is the frozen one
```

Fix: identify the tiles by the gate itself instead of by position — it's also a stronger assertion of the actual contract (exactly one live swapper):

```dart
KaomojiFace shown(bool liveActive) =>
    (tester.widget(find.descendant(
      of: find.byWidgetPredicate(
          (w) => w is KaomojiSwapper && w.active == liveActive),
      matching: find.byWidgetPredicate((w) => w.key is ValueKey<KaomojiFace>),
    )).key! as ValueKey<KaomojiFace>).value;

expect(tester.widgetList<KaomojiSwapper>(find.byType(KaomojiSwapper)),
    hasLength(2));
final liveBefore = shown(true);
final finishedBefore = shown(false);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
expect(shown(false), same(finishedBefore),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face');
expect(shown(true), isNot(same(liveBefore)),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');
```

(`KaomojiSwapper` is public through the `fa_ui` barrel; matching by the `active` flag is stable across the boundary rebuild, unlike widget-instance lookups.)

Everything else in the rework verified green: the two finder fixes pass, `liveThinkingMessage` unit test passes, CLI kaomoji tests 23/23, core spec tests 10/10, analyzer clean on all touched files.

The only red test in the package is this PR's new `wiring (AC4)` test. A runtime probe of the exact same tree (two thinking tiles through the real `FaChatScreen`, one pump past the swap boundary) shows **the gate itself works**:

```
PROBE swappers mounted: 2   active flags: [true, false]
PROBE face[0] moved across the boundary  (the LIVE tile)
PROBE face[1] identical before/after     (the finished note — frozen)
```

The transcript list renders **newest-first in tree order** (reversed display list), so `_faces[0]` is the LIVE thinking tile and `_faces[1]` is the finished note — the exact opposite of what the assertions assume:

```dart
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
final after = _faces(tester);
expect(after[0], same(before[0]),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face'); // ← [0] IS the live tile
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');            // ← [1] is the frozen one
```

Fix: identify the tiles by the gate itself instead of by position — it's also a stronger assertion of the actual contract (exactly one live swapper):

```dart
KaomojiFace shown(bool liveActive) =>
    (tester.widget(find.descendant(
      of: find.byWidgetPredicate(
          (w) => w is KaomojiSwapper && w.active == liveActive),
      matching: find.byWidgetPredicate((w) => w.key is ValueKey<KaomojiFace>),
    )).key! as ValueKey<KaomojiFace>).value;

expect(tester.widgetList<KaomojiSwapper>(find.byType(KaomojiSwapper)),
    hasLength(2));
final liveBefore = shown(true);
final finishedBefore = shown(false);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
expect(shown(false), same(finishedBefore),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face');
expect(shown(true), isNot(same(liveBefore)),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');
```

(`KaomojiSwapper` is public through the `fa_ui` barrel; matching by the `active` flag is stable across the boundary rebuild, unlike widget-instance lookups.)

The only red test in the package is this PR's new `wiring (AC4)` test. A runtime probe of the exact same tree (two thinking tiles through the real `FaChatScreen`, one pump past the swap boundary) shows **the gate itself works**:

```
PROBE swappers mounted: 2   active flags: [true, false]
PROBE face[0] moved across the boundary  (the LIVE tile)
PROBE face[1] identical before/after     (the finished note — frozen)
```

The transcript list renders **newest-first in tree order** (reversed display list), so `_faces[0]` is the LIVE thinking tile and `_faces[1]` is the finished note — the exact opposite of what the assertions assume:

```dart
final before = _faces(tester);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
final after = _faces(tester);
expect(after[0], same(before[0]),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face'); // ← [0] IS the live tile
expect(after[1], isNot(same(before[1])),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');            // ← [1] is the frozen one
```

Fix: identify the tiles by the gate itself instead of by position — it's also a stronger assertion of the actual contract (exactly one live swapper):

```dart
KaomojiFace shown(bool liveActive) =>
    (tester.widget(find.descendant(
      of: find.byWidgetPredicate(
          (w) => w is KaomojiSwapper && w.active == liveActive),
      matching: find.byWidgetPredicate((w) => w.key is ValueKey<KaomojiFace>),
    )).key! as ValueKey<KaomojiFace>).value;

expect(tester.widgetList<KaomojiSwapper>(find.byType(KaomojiSwapper)),
    hasLength(2));
final liveBefore = shown(true);
final finishedBefore = shown(false);
await tester.pump(kKaomojiSwapPeriod);
expect(shown(false), same(finishedBefore),
    reason: 'the finished thinking note keeps its frozen face');
expect(shown(true), isNot(same(liveBefore)),
    reason: 'only the LIVE thinking block animates');
```

(`KaomojiSwapper` is public through the `fa_ui` barrel; matching by the `active` flag is stable across the boundary rebuild, unlike widget-instance lookups.)
